mainTopic: Making an עירוב for a city: splitting it into halves, separate alleyways, the number of entrances, and the status of a ladder
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about making an עירוב for a city and then works through several of its lines. First the גמרא asks which תנא allows an עירוב for a city with a רשות הרבים running through it. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that it is רבי יהודה, who lets a person close off a public street with a לחי or קורה, while the חכמים disagree. Next comes the ברייתא's rule that a city may not get an עירוב in halves. In one version, רב פפא allows a split across the width, and even רבי עקיבא could agree because each half has its own gate. In a second version, רב פפא forbids any split, and even the רבנן could agree because the public road cannot be shut off. The גמרא then explains that separate עירובין for each מבוי work when the alleys put up a דקה, backed by a teaching of רב חסדא. A story follows in which אביי shows רבי זירא that a town needs a שיור once a garbage heap blocking its second entrance is cleared. Finally, רב נחמן teaches that a ladder counts as a wall at the end of an area but as an entrance between two courtyards. The גמרא then begins a challenge to רב נחמן that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: a public city with one entrance can have one עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by ruling that if a city with public status has only one entrance, one עירוב can cover the whole city.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it has only one entrance, we may make an עירוב for all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the last line of a ברייתא that started on the previous page. It says that a public city with only one entrance can get a single עירוב for the whole city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A city with just one entrance is closed in on all other sides, so it does not work like an open public road that people pass through. That is why one עירוב can include everyone. The rest of this ברייתא, which allows an עירוב even where a רשות הרבים passes through a city, is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: We make an עירוב (joining the residents so they may carry)
All of it, the entire city

phrases.english: and it has only one entrance —
phrases.notes: Continuation of the ברייתא from the previous page

phrases.english: we may make an eiruv for all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public city with only one entrance may have a single עירוב for the entire city.

steps.title: Who holds that an עירוב can work for a public road?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא would allow an עירוב for a city that has a רשות הרבים running through it, as the ברייתא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that an עירוב can be made for a public domain?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows, since it allows an עירוב for a public road. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a true רשות הרבים cannot be made into a private area just by putting up small markers like a לחי or a קורה. The ברייתא seems to allow this, so the גמרא wants to know which תנא is behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא? (whose opinion is this?)
Public domain, a main public road

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
who holds that a public domain can be given an eiruv?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the authorship of the ברייתא just completed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא allows an עירוב (using a לחי or קורה) for an area that includes a רשות הרבים

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said: It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the question: the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. Proof of this comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming רבי יהודה tells us the ברייתא is not the majority view. Most תנאים would not allow an עירוב for a public road.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2

steps.title: רבי יהודה lets a person close off a public street between his two houses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה lets someone with houses on both sides of a public road put up a לחי or קורה at each end and then carry in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Moreover, רבי יהודה said: Someone who has two houses on the two sides of the public domain may put a לחי on this side and a לחי on that side, or a קורה here and a קורה there, and then carry in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the answer from a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה allows a public street to be made into a private carrying area using only a לחי or a קורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה lets small symbolic markers turn part of a public road into a private area, he clearly holds that a רשות הרבים can be given an עירוב. That matches the ברייתא about the city. This is the source for רב הונא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A post standing at the side of an opening
A beam placed across the top of an opening
In the middle, in the area between

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Moreover, Rabbi Yehuda said:
One who has two houses
on two sides of the public domain —
may make a post here and a post there,
or a beam here and a beam there,
and he may carry in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה allows an עירוב for a רשות הרבים
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא in which רבי יהודה allows a לחי or קורה at both ends of a public street between one's two houses

steps.title: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה that a public domain cannot be given an עירוב in this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: One may not make an עירוב for a public domain in this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the חכמים rejecting רבי יהודה's view. This confirms that allowing an עירוב in a public road is רבי יהודה's own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the חכמים disagree, the city ברייתא cannot be everyone's view. It must follow רבי יהודה, exactly as רב הונא said.
steps.whatToRemember: The city ברייתא allows an עירוב for an area with a public road. That fits only רבי יהודה, who allows a לחי or קורה to work even in a רשות הרבים. The חכמים say it does not work.

phrases.english: They said to him:
One may not make an eiruv for a public domain in this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְעָרְבִין רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the quoted ברייתא with the dissenting view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a לחי or קורה cannot make a רשות הרבים into a place covered by an עירוב.

steps.title: No עירוב in halves only applies when the city is split lengthwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that a city cannot get an עירוב in halves. רב פפא limits it: splitting lengthwise is forbidden, but splitting across the width is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'And we do not make an עירוב for it in halves.' רב פפא said: They said this only about its length, but across its width we may make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote another line of the city ברייתא, about not giving a city an עירוב in halves. רב פפא then narrows that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the city is split lengthwise, the public road runs through both halves and both sides use the whole road, so the road ties them together. If it is split across the width, each half mainly uses its own section of the road. So each half can have its own עירוב.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. Splitting along the length of the public road is the forbidden case. Cutting across its width is the permitted case.

phrases.english: The Master said:
And one may not make an eiruv for it in halves.
Rav Pappa said:
They said this only regarding its length,
but regarding its width — one may make an eiruv.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְאֵין מְעָרְבִין אוֹתָהּ לַחֲצָאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to explain a different clause of it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on giving a city an עירוב in halves applies only to a lengthwise split. A split across the width is allowed.

steps.title: Whose view does רב פפא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's opinion רב פפא's ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion fits רב פפא's leniency about splitting a city across its width. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Allowing a split across the width assumes that one half's residents walking through the other half does not ruin that half's עירוב. Not every תנא accepts that assumption.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind רב פפא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view supports allowing a widthwise split

steps.title: Not like רבי עקיבא, whose 'foot' rule would forbid it
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's ruling does not follow רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא holds that a 'foot' allowed in its own area still forbids carrying in an area that is not its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not in accordance with רבי עקיבא. For if it were like רבי עקיבא, he said: A foot that is permitted in its own place forbids even in a place that is not its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא's ruling does not follow רבי עקיבא, and it explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a city is split across its width, people from one half still walk through the other half's section of the road. They are allowed to carry in their own half but not in the other half. רבי עקיבא holds that such a 'foot', with a right to pass through, forbids carrying in the place it passes through, so he would not allow the split.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'foot': a person's right to walk through an area
That is permitted (to carry) in its own place
In a place that is not its own

steps.whyThisMatters: This suggestion ties רב פפא's leniency to the dispute about whether a passer-through who cannot carry there ruins another area's עירוב. The next step shows that this link does not hold.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only a first suggestion. רבי עקיבא holds that a 'foot' permitted in its own place still forbids even where it is not its own, so at first רב פפא's leniency seems to go against him. The next step rejects this and shows that even רבי עקיבא could agree with רב פפא.

phrases.english: not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.
For if it were in accordance with Rabbi Akiva,
didn't he say:
a foot that is permitted in its own place —
prohibits even in a place that is not its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 and explains its reasoning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא's ruling does not follow רבי עקיבא, because by רבי עקיבא's 'foot' rule the residents passing through would forbid carrying in the other half.

steps.title: Even רבי עקיבא could agree with רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on the claim that רב פפא cannot follow רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא spoke only about an inner courtyard that has no other exit. In a city, each half can leave through its own gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say רב פפא follows רבי עקיבא, there is no problem. רבי עקיבא said his rule only about two courtyards, one inside the other. The inner courtyard has no other way out, so its people must walk through the outer one. But here, in the city, these people go out through this gate, and those people go out through that gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea from step 8 that רב פפא's ruling cannot fit רבי עקיבא. It shows that רבי עקיבא's case is different from the case of a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי עקיבא's case, the people of the inner courtyard have no choice. They must pass through the outer courtyard, so they really share it and can forbid carrying there. A city split across its width is different, because each half has its own gate and does not need the other half's part of the road. So each half does not forbid carrying in the other half.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (a way of showing that even this opinion could work)
He only said his rule in this case (he limits the opinion to its own case)
One inside the other (an inner courtyard behind an outer courtyard)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that רבי עקיבא's rule about the 'foot' is being rejected here. The rule still stands. The גמרא is only saying that it does not apply to a city, where each half has its own way out.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Rabbi Akiva:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only said his rule there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת זוֹ לְפָנִים מִזּוֹ,
phrases.english: in the case of two courtyards, one inside the other,
because the inner one has no other entrance.
phrases.notes: So its people must pass through the outer courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, הָנֵי נָפְקִי בְּהַאי פִּיתְחָא,
phrases.english: But here, these people go out through this gate,
and those people go out through that gate.
phrases.notes: Each half of the city has its own city gate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's claim that רב פפא cannot fit רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב פפא's lenient ruling about splitting across the width goes against רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא's rule depends on the inner courtyard having no other exit. A city split across its width does not have that problem, because each half has its own gate.

steps.title: Second version: no split at all, even across the width
steps.stepSummary: Some say רב פפא said the opposite: a city cannot get an עירוב in halves, whether it is split along its length or across its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version. רב פפא said: Do not think that only a split along the length is forbidden while a split across the width is allowed. Even a split across the width is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב פפא's statement. In this version he is strict about both kinds of split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, splitting across the width was allowed. In this version, any split of the city into halves for an עירוב is forbidden. This new version sets up the question in the next step: which תנא does it follow?
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion that argues with רב פפא. It is a different report of what רב פפא himself said.

phrases.english: Some say: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא לְאׇרְכָּהּ הוּא דְּלָא מְעָרְבִין,
phrases.english: Do not say that only along its length we may not make an eiruv,
but across its width we may make an eiruv,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לְרׇחְבָּהּ נָמֵי לָא מְעָרְבִין.
phrases.english: rather, even across its width we may not make an eiruv.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב פפא's ruling from step 6, this time strict for both kinds of split.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city may not get an עירוב in halves, not along its length and not across its width.

steps.title: Does the strict version follow only רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the strict version follows, and suggests that it must be רבי עקיבא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It seems to be רבי עקיבא's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the strict version of רב פפא follows. It suggests that this sounds like רבי עקיבא, who holds that one group's 'foot' can forbid carrying for another group. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא is the strict one in the courtyard case, so a strict ruling seems to match him. That would mean the רבנן disagree with this version of רב פפא. The next step will challenge that idea.

phrases.english: Following whom? It follows Rabbi Akiva!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which תנא the second version in step 10 follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the strict version of רב פפא follows, with the suggestion that it can only be רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Even the רבנן could agree with the strict version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even the רבנן could hold the strict view. In the courtyard case, the inner courtyard can close its door. But nobody can take the public road away from the people of the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it follows the רבנן, there is no problem. The רבנן said their rule only about two courtyards, one inside the other. There, the people of the inner courtyard can close the door and use only their own courtyard. But here, can they move the public road away from here?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the strict version must follow רבי עקיבא. It shows that the רבנן's lenient rule does not apply to a city.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן are lenient with courtyards because the inner courtyard can shut its door and keep to itself. In a city, the public road stays open to everyone, and the people of one half cannot be stopped from using the other half. So even the רבנן would agree that an עירוב for half a city does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, here the city's public road

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב פפא. In the first, a split across the width is allowed, and even רבי עקיבא agrees because each half has its own gate. In the second, no split is allowed, and even the רבנן agree because the public road cannot be closed off.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם
phrases.english: the Rabbis only said their rule there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ,
phrases.english: in the case of two courtyards, one inside the other,
because the inner one can close the door and use its own space.
But here, are they able to remove
the public domain from here?!
phrases.notes: No. Everyone keeps using the whole public road.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 11 that the strict version can only follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the strict version of רב פפא must follow רבי עקיבא and goes against the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן's leniency depends on the inner courtyard being able to shut itself off. A city's public road cannot be shut off from the residents.

steps.title: Why is a separate עירוב for each מבוי allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא, which allows an עירוב either for the whole city or for each מבוי separately. It asks: if halves forbid each other, why don't separate alleyways also forbid each other?
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said in the ברייתא: an עירוב is made either for the whole city, or for each alleyway by itself. What is different about halves, which are not allowed? The reason is that the halves forbid carrying for each other. But alleyways also forbid carrying for each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the wording of the ברייתא and raises a challenge. If halves of a city cannot have separate עירובין because they forbid each other, the same problem should exist for separate alleyways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Halves are forbidden because the people of each half use the other half's area, so they forbid carrying there. People of one מבוי also walk into other alleyways. So the reason that rules out halves seems to rule out alleyways too. That is why the ברייתא's permission for separate alleyways is being questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that opens onto courtyards
They forbid carrying for each other

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אוֹ כּוּלָּהּ, אוֹ מָבוֹי מָבוֹי בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: The master said: Either for all of it, or each alleyway by itself.
What is different about halves, which are not allowed?
Because they forbid each other.
Each alleyway also forbids the others!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אוֹ כּוּלָּהּ, אוֹ מָבוֹי מָבוֹי בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב פפא discussion and returns to the ברייתא's ruling quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a separate עירוב for each מבוי is allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Halves are not allowed because they forbid each other. People of separate alleyways also use each other's space, so they should forbid each other in the same way.

steps.title: The alleyways put up a partition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that allows a separate עירוב for each מבוי is talking about a case where the residents put up a דקה to show their alley is separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, what case are we dealing with? A case where they made a small partition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13. The ברייתא is talking about alleyways that have marked themselves off with a partition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, separate groups in one city could forbid each other, just like the two halves do. But when an alley puts up a דקה at its entrance, it shows that it gives up any connection to the other alleys. So the alleys no longer forbid each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (a formula that narrows a source down to a specific case)
A small partition or marker at an entrance, showing separation

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
Such as where they made a small partition.
phrases.notes: The partition shows that the alley wants to be separate from the rest of the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separate alleyways should forbid each other, just like the city's halves do.
steps.terutzMaskana: Alleyways that put up a דקה have given up their connection to each other, so they do not forbid each other.

steps.title: Support from רב חסדא about a partition
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a resident who puts up a דקה at his own doorway does not forbid the rest of the alley.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב חסדא: if one of the residents of an alley made a partition at his doorway, he does not forbid the other residents of the alley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רב חסדא to back up the idea that a דקה separates a person from the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is talking about one person, but the logic is the same. A partition shows that someone does not want to use the shared area. Once he shows that, he does not stop the others from carrying. The same works for a whole alley that marks itself off.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: And it is like that which Rav Idi bar Avin said
Rav Chisda said:
One of the residents of an alleyway
who made a partition at his doorway
does not forbid the residents of the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 14 with a parallel ruling
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a דקה separates a person or group, so they do not forbid others
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling about one resident who makes a דקה at his doorway
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the principle behind the answer: a physical sign of separation removes a person's power to forbid others in an עירוב.

steps.title: רבי זירא includes the whole town in the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, about a public city. Then it tells how רבי זירא made an עירוב for רבי חייא's town without leaving out a שיור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'If it was a public city and it is still public, etc.' רבי זירא made an עירוב for the town of רבי חייא's family and did not leave out any section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line of the ברייתא about public cities. It tells a story that sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a public city must leave out some section, called a שיור, when making an עירוב. רבי זירא did not leave out anything. That looks like he was treating the town as a city that started out private, and it raises an obvious question.

keyTerms.meaning: A public city (a city that belongs to the public)
He made an עירוב for it
A section deliberately left out of the עירוב

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה שֶׁל רַבִּים וַהֲרֵי הִיא כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: If it was a public city and it is still public, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote of the ברייתא that opens a new topic.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira made an eruv for it
for the town of Rabbi Chiyya's family
and did not leave out any section of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא made an עירוב for the whole town of רבי חייא without leaving a שיור.

steps.title: אביי asks why there was no שיור
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבי זירא why he did not leave out a section of the town.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why did the Master do this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions what רבי זירא did. He asks what his reason was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for the reason, not yet an attack. Behind it is an assumption: this town seems to be a public city, and a public city needs a שיור.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (a polite way to address a scholar)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is the reason the Master acted this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the act in Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי זירא did not leave a שיור when making the town's עירוב

steps.title: רבי זירא relies on what the elders reported
steps.stepSummary: The elders told רבי זירא that רב חייא בר אסי used to include the whole town. From this he concluded it was a private city that became public.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The town's elders told me that רב חייא בר אסי used to make an עירוב for all of it. I said to myself: learn from this that it is a city that started private and became public.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains himself. He relied on an earlier practice and drew a conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A city that started as private and later became public may have one עירוב for the whole city, with no שיור. רבי זירא figured that רב חייא בר אסי's practice only made sense if this town was that kind of city.

keyTerms.term: עִיר שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל רַבִּים
keyTerms.meaning: A city that belonged to one person and later became public

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, סָבֵי דִּידַהּ אָמְרִי לִי:
phrases.english: He said to him: Its elders told me:

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַסִּי מְעָרֵב כּוּלַּהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Asi used to make an eruv for all of it.
And I said: Learn from this

phrases.aramaic: עִיר שֶׁל יָחִיד וְנַעֲשֵׂית שֶׁל רַבִּים הִיא.
phrases.english: that it is a city of an individual that became public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Based on רב חייא בר אסי's practice, רבי זירא assumed the town started private and became public, so no שיור is needed.

steps.title: The real reason was a garbage heap
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that the same elders told him the real reason. A garbage heap blocked one entrance, leaving one entrance. Now that it has been cleared, the town has two entrances and a whole-town עירוב is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Those elders told me that there was a garbage heap on one side of the town. Now that the garbage heap has been cleared away, the town has two entrances, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבי זירא's conclusion. He gives a different explanation for רב חייא בר אסי's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A public city with only one entrance may be included in the עירוב as a whole. The garbage heap blocked the second entrance, which is why רב חייא בר אסי could include everything. Now that the heap is gone, the town has two entrances again, so it needs a שיור.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying רב חייא בר אסי was wrong. His practice was correct when it was made. The facts changed afterward.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, לְדִידִי אֲמַרוּ לִי הָנְהוּ סָבֵי:
phrases.english: He said to him: Those same elders told me:

phrases.aramaic: הַהִיא אַשְׁפָּה הֲוָה לַהּ מֵחַד גִּיסָא.
phrases.english: There was a garbage heap on one side of it.
And now that the garbage heap has been cleared away,
it has two entrances, and it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion רבי זירא drew in Step 18
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי זירא's conclusion that the town started private and became public
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב חייא בר אסי's practice rested on there being one entrance, because the garbage heap blocked the other. It did not depend on how the city started. Now that the heap is gone, a שיור is needed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the number of entrances can decide whether a public city needs a שיור, and that a past practice must be checked against the current facts.

steps.title: רבי זירא admits he did not know
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the situation was not known to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It was not on my mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא accepts אביי's correction. He explains that he simply did not know about the garbage heap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא does not argue with the rule. He admits his mistake came from not knowing the facts. The conclusion is that this town now needs a שיור.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not on my mind (I did not know)

steps.whatToRemember: A public city may be included in the עירוב as a whole only if it is a private city that became public, or if it has just one entrance. Once a blocked second entrance is opened, a שיור must be left out.

phrases.english: He said to him: It was not on my mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the correction from Step 19
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's whole-town עירוב came from not knowing the facts. Now that the town has two entrances, it needs a שיור.

steps.title: A ladder on one side and an entrance on the other
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי בר אדא from הרפניא asks רבה about a town or area with a ladder on one side and an entrance on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי בר אדא from הרפניא asked רבה: If there is a ladder on one side and an entrance on the other side, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. Someone asks רבה whether a ladder on one side counts like a second entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that a town with two entrances is treated as public, so an עירוב for the whole town is forbidden without leaving out a שיור. Now the question is about a ladder. If a ladder counts as an entrance, the place has two openings. If it does not count, the place has only one.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a question of law)

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַמֵּי בַּר אַדָּא הַרְפַּנָּאָה מֵרַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Ami bar Adda of Harpanya asked Rabba:
A ladder on this side and an entrance on that side, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The question is whether the ladder makes the place count as open on both ends.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַמֵּי בַּר אַדָּא הַרְפַּנָּאָה מֵרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea from Step 19 that the number of entrances decides whether a whole-town עירוב is allowed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a ladder count as an entrance, making the place open on two sides?

steps.title: רבה: a ladder counts as an entrance
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers in the name of רב that a ladder has the status of an entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: This is what רב said: A ladder has the status of an entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by quoting רב: a ladder counts as an entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer, the place counts as open on both sides. So it would be treated like a place with two entrances.

keyTerms.meaning: It has the legal status of an entrance

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav said:
A ladder has the status of an entrance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ladder is treated as an entrance, so the place counts as open on both sides.

steps.title: רב נחמן: that is not the full quote
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells them not to listen to רבה, and gives a fuller version of רב's teaching: a ladder can be either an entrance or a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: Do not listen to him. This is what רב אדא said in the name of רב: A ladder has the status of an entrance, and it also has the status of a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן rejects רבה's report. He says רב actually taught that a ladder is sometimes an entrance and sometimes a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה quoted only half of רב's teaching. According to רב נחמן, the ladder does not always count as an entrance. The next step explains which case is which.

keyTerms.meaning: It has the legal status of a wall

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying רב never called a ladder an entrance. He is saying it depends on the case, and our case (the town) is not one where it counts as an entrance.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן: לָא תְּצִיתוּ לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them: Do not listen to him,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב אַדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: this is what Rav Adda said in the name of Rav:
A ladder has the status of an entrance,
and it has the status of a wall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן: לָא תְּצִיתוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's version of רב's teaching from Step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that, according to רב, a ladder always counts as an entrance.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבה's quote was incomplete. רב taught that a ladder has two possible statuses.

steps.title: When a ladder is a wall and when it is an entrance
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains: in our case (the end of the town or area) the ladder is a wall. Between two courtyards it is an entrance, so they may make one עירוב or two.
steps.simpleTranslation: It has the status of a wall in the case we just mentioned. It has the status of an entrance when the ladder stands between two courtyards: if they want, they make one עירוב together; if they want, the two courtyards each make their own עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains the two halves of רב's teaching. In the case of the town, the ladder counts as a wall. Between two courtyards, it counts as an entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the town case, the ladder does not create a second opening, so the place is closed on that side. Between two courtyards, the ladder is enough of an opening to let them join into one עירוב. They may still choose to make separate ones.

keyTerms.meaning: As we said (referring back to our case)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a ladder at the end of a town or area counts as a wall, not a second entrance. A ladder between two courtyards counts as an entrance, so they may choose one shared עירוב or two separate ones.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same object can get different legal statuses depending on what question we are asking. Here the questions are "Is this area closed?" and "Can these two places join together?"

phrases.english: It has the status of a wall, as we said.
phrases.notes: In the case of the ladder on one side, the ladder closes that side.

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרַת פֶּתַח עָלָיו, בְּסוּלָּם שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת,
phrases.english: It has the status of an entrance in the case of a ladder between two courtyards,
if they want, they make one eiruv,
if they want, the two make separate eiruvin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two-sided teaching that רב נחמן introduced in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ladder at the end of the area counts as a wall. A ladder between two courtyards counts as an entrance, so they may make one עירוב or two.

steps.title: Did רב נחמן really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to challenge רב נחמן from another teaching he quoted from שמואל, about courtyard residents and balcony residents who forgot to make an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב נחמן really say this? But רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: The residents of a courtyard and the residents of a balcony who forgot...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It is about to quote another statement of רב נחמן that seems to contradict what he just said about ladders, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that רב נחמן seems to say two different things. Here he says a ladder between two areas counts as an entrance. The case of the courtyard and the balcony, which is cut off mid-sentence, will show a different view.

phrases.english: Did Rav Nachman really say this?
But Rav Nachman said in the name of Shmuel:
The residents of a courtyard and the residents of a balcony who forgot
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's teaching from Steps 23–24 by pointing to another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a ladder can count as an entrance between two areas.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another statement רב נחמן quoted from שמואל, about a courtyard and a balcony, seems to contradict it. The full contradiction is finished on the next amud.
